thread:
lina: hey team — running the CLI quickstart in a Docker image and my first call fails with 502, but the dashboard accepts the token. any hints?

lina: command: `docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY sample/quickstart`
```
> POST /v1/chat
> Authorization: Bearer ***
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\ncontent-type: text/html\n\n<html>502 Bad Gateway</html>
```

lina: key is definitely in the container env. not a 401/403. dashboard quickstart shows success.
devon: is that a workspace token or a service key? 502 usually indicates a proxy/routing failure, not auth.
lina: using a workspace token from Settings -> API tokens. tried a service key and got 403, but workspace token yields 502.
maya: we've seen corp proxies that strip `Authorization` header. the SDK ends up retrying and some upstream layer returns 502 instead of 402/401.
onboard-bot: Your org (acme-staging) does not have an active billing method on file. First outbound calls may be gated. https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme-staging/billing
lina: odd — dashboard accepted the token without showing billing modal. inconsistent UX.
devon: can you reproduce with curl locally? `curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"hi"}'`
lina: outside Docker I get 402 Payment Required: `{\"error\":\"org_billing_required\"}`. inside Docker it's 502.
devon: that matches header stripping. the container (or your corporate network) probably removes Authorization. SDK retries then hit a different routing path -> 502.
maya: workaround: mount the token file and read it inside container or pass it via `-e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat ~/.redwood/service_key)`. CLI/SDK should also detect this class of 502 and present the billing-required message.
lina: confirmed: passing the key via `-e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat ~/.redwood/service_key)` returns the JSON 402 pointing to billing.
lina: repro notes: 1) org without billing on file 2) use workspace token vs service key 3) run inside environment that strips headers (corp docker/proxy) 4) observe 502 instead of 402.
devon: please open an eng/devex ticket with the minimal Dockerfile, run command, and natted headers. proposed actions: 1) make SDK/CLI map known 502 patterns to 402 with actionable text, 2) add docs about proxies removing Authorization, 3) surface onboarding hint when dashboard quickstart hides billing state.
maya: I'll draft a small doc + suggested CLI error text: "Payment required — add billing at <link>. If running behind a proxy, ensure Authorization header is preserved or pass a service key file."
lina: filing issue and attaching logs/run steps now. tagging @devon @maya. thanks! :thumbsup:
